title: SeqPhase Sherpa: sequence-length + architecture-aware kernel curator and online autotuner
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Kernel performance varies dramatically by architecture (A100/RTX/TPU-like) and by sequence phase (long prefill vs short decode). We need a lightweight curator that picks and fast-adapts kernel variants per request cohort to reduce p99 latency tail and average token cost without increasing rollback risk.

This ticket implements 'SeqPhase Sherpa', a runtime-side kernel curator that: (1) classifies incoming requests into compact phase-aware fingerprints (prefill length distribution, decode steps, model variant, quantization profile, hw arch), (2) consults a small curated candidate set of kernel implementations (memory-layout + attention algorithm variants), (3) runs an online lightweight autotuner (bandit-style / Thompson sampling with safety guardrails) to pick per-cohort kernels, and (4) exposes telemetry and an emergency fallback when latency or error rate drifts.

Goals: reduce token-cost by 8-15% on mixed workloads, reduce p99 latency by 10-25% for decode-heavy bursts, and maintain determinism for safety-critical customers via pinning and audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: Sherpa runs in the serving runtime as a configurable policy module (opt-in)
Identification fingerprints produced with <2ms overhead per request and <5% additional memory footprint
Online tuner can explore/roll back without violating configured latency SLOs (safety margin configurable)
Benchmarks: mixed workload (prefill-heavy + chat) shows >=8% token-cost reduction or >=10% p99 latency improvement on at least two architectures (A100, RTX6000)
Dashboard: per-cohort kernel choice, success rate, latency distribution, and tuning decisions visible in Console
E2E regression tests and chaos tests (fallback on kernel OOM/incorrect outputs) added to CI
implementation_steps: Design fingerprint schema (features: mean prefill length, decode-step histogram, model opset, quantization, batch-size, hw-arch) — capture in design doc
Implement low-cost fingerprint extractor and canonicalizer in runtime (C++ path + python shim for test harness)
Define candidate kernel manifests and compatibility matrix; add metadata for memory/cost/latency profiles
Prototype online tuner using Thompson-sampling bandit with safety constraints and exponential backoff on rejects
Integrate tuner decisions into kernel dispatch path with a fast cache and TTL; ensure atomic switch/rollback semantics
Add telemetry hooks (decision_id, cohort_id, chosen_kernel, metric snapshots) and wire into Console event stream
Run offline replay experiments on production traces to seed priors and candidate ranking
Create canary rollout plan, run in dedicated pool, monitor regressions, and iterate
risks: Exploration may transiently increase latency for a subset of customers if safety margins are misconfigured
Fingerprint collision may mix incompatible workloads; need conservative default grouping
Kernel correctness bugs can be masked by fallback — must ensure deterministic test coverage per kernel variant
State explosion if too many cohorts are created — require cohort cardinality cap and TTL eviction
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint extractor and compatibility checks
Microbench harness for each kernel variant across architectures and seq-len buckets
Replay-based A/B experiments on historical traffic with simulated bandit to validate priors
Canary in dedicated Dedicated pool with automatic rollback if p95/p99 exceeds configured SLO
Chaos test: force kernel OOM/bad return and validate fallback and audit logging

notes: Design choices: prefer smaller candidate sets per cohort (3-5 kernels) to limit risk and storage. Use exponential backoff on failing candidates.
Operational: default Sherpa policy is opt-in per customer; enterprise customers can pin kernel manifests to freeze behavior for compliance.
Future: if Sherpa shows value, plan to expose recommended quantization+kernel profiles in Redwood Optimize
